domain_summary.content: Cognitive tasks assess how your child thinks, reacts, and learns about the world.

content: Infants are given tasks that measure their interest in new things, their attention to familiar and unfamiliar objects, and how they play with different types of toys.
Toddlers are given tasks that examine how they explore new toys and experiences, how they solve problems, how they learn, and their ability to complete puzzles.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 8 in the cognitive domain, corresponding to an age equivalent of 8 months. This places her in the below average range, reflecting an estimated 20% delay relative to her chronological age of 10 months. During the assessment, Sabrina displayed limited engagement with new objects and required additional time to initiate exploratory play. These findings suggest a need for interventions focused on enhancing cognitive and exploratory skills.

domain_summary.content: Receptive Communication tasks assess how well your child recognizes sounds and how much she understands spoken words and directions.

content: Infants are presented with tasks that measure their recognition of sounds, objects, and people in the environment. Many tasks involve social interactions.
Toddlers are asked to identify pictures and objects, follow simple directions, and perform social routines, such as wave bye-bye or play peek-a-boo.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 9 in the receptive communication domain, with an age equivalent of 9 months. This places her in the average range, indicating a 10% delay. Sabrina responded well to familiar sounds but exhibited less consistent responses to spoken requests. Continued focus on enhancing her receptive language through engaging activities is recommended.

domain_summary.content: Expressive Communication tasks assess how well your child communicates using sounds, gestures, or words.

content: Infants are observed throughout the assessment for various forms of nonverbal expression, such as smiling, jabbering expressively, using gestures, and laughing (social interaction).
Toddlers are given opportunities to use words by naming objects or pictures, putting words together, and answering questions.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 7, with an age equivalent of 7 months. This places her in the below average range, reflecting a 30% delay. Sabrina primarily relied on gestures and vocalizations, exhibiting limited verbal expression. Participation in activities promoting language emergence would be beneficial.

domain_summary.content: Fine Motor tasks assess how well your child can use their hands and fingers to make things happen.

content: Muscle control is assessed in infants, such as visual tracking with their eyes, bringing a hand to their mouth, transferring objects from hand to hand, and reaching for and grasping an object.
Toddlers are given the opportunity to demonstrate their ability to perform fine motor tasks, such as stacking blocks, drawing simple shapes, and placing small objects (e.g., coins) in a slot.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 8, with an age equivalent of 8 months. This places her in the below average range, reflecting a 20% delay. Observations noted difficulty with object manipulation and sustained grasp. Interventions targeting fine motor strength and coordination are advised.

domain_summary.content: Gross Motor tasks assess how well your child can move their body.

content: Infants are assessed for head control and their performance on activities, such as rolling over, sitting upright, and crawling motions.
Toddlers are given tasks that measure their ability to make stepping movements, support their own weight, stand, and walk without assistance.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 6, with an age equivalent of 6 months. This places her in the below average range, reflecting a 40% delay. She demonstrated challenges with maintaining stability during sitting and transitioning to crawling. Emphasizing gross motor skill development at home and through therapy can support her progress in mobility.

domain_summary.content: The Social-Emotional Scale asks caregivers to assess how their child interacts with others, expresses emotions, and responds to sensory input such as sounds, touch, and visual stimuli. This scale helps identify age-appropriate social-emotional milestones related to attachment, self-regulation, and engagement in early relationships.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 9 and a standard score of 90 on the Social-Emotional domain, placing her in the average range and reflecting approximately a 10% delay relative to her chronological age of 10 months. According to caregiver report, Sabrina engages with familiar caregivers but displays hesitation in novel social settings. These observations suggest potential support in fostering social engagement and adaptive interaction skills within various environments.

domain_summary.content: The Adaptive Behavior Scale asks caregivers to assess their child's ability to adapt to various demands of normal daily living and become more independent.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina's adaptive functioning was assessed through caregiver report using the Bayley-4 Adaptive Behavior Scales. Her Adaptive Behavior Composite (ADBE) score was 85, which places her performance in the below average range and reflects a 15% delay compared to her chronological age.

receptive_communication.content: Sabrina earned a scaled score of 9, with an age equivalent of 9 months, reflecting a 10% delay. She consistently recognizes and responds to familiar voices and can follow simple instructions.

expressive_communication.content: She received a scaled score of 7, with an age equivalent of 7 months, indicating a 30% delay. Sabrina primarily uses single sounds and gestures to communicate needs.

personal_self_care.content: In this domain, Sabrina received a scaled score of 8, with an age equivalent of 8 months, reflecting a 20% delay. She shows emerging self-feeding skills but requires assistance with most self-care activities.

interpersonal_relationships.content: Sabrina earned a scaled score of 8, with an age equivalent of 8 months, reflecting a 20% delay. She is able to express basic needs and emotions but may need support with more complex social interactions.

play_and_leisure.content: In this domain, Sabrina received a scaled score of 7, with an age equivalent of 7 months, indicating a 30% delay. She engages in simple solitary play and shows limited interest in interactive games.
